Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 05-Feb-2025 (01:00 PM - 04:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIRST SEMESTER B.TECH. (CORE STREAM) EXAMINATIONS - FEBRUARY 2025  
  SUBJECT: BIO_1071 BIOLOGY FOR ENGINEERS  
  (MAKEUP)  
  Biology for Engineers [BIO-1071]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                      Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  ABC  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               Compare carbon with other potential backbone elements, such as silicon. Why is carbon preferred          (3)  
  in biological systems, despite silicon's ability to also form four bonds?  
1B)               How does the high specific heat capacity of water contribute to its effectiveness as a                   (3)  
  thermoregulator in the human body? What implications does this property have for maintaining  
  homeostasis during extreme environmental conditions?  
1C)               In winter, you went to buy coconut oil, sunflower oil, palm oil, and olive oil. You noticed that coconut (4)  
  oil and palm oil were cloudy and appeared solidified, while olive oil and sunflower oil remained clear  
  and liquid. At a second store, you observed the same phenomenon. How would you explain this?  
2A)               A couple has four children. Neither the father nor the mother is bald; one of the two sons is bald, (3)  
  but neither of the daughters is bald.  
  (a) If one of the daughters marries a non-bald man and they have a son, what is the chance that the  
  son will become bald as an adult?  
  (b) If the couple has a daughter, what is the chance that she will become bald as an adult?  
  (1½+1½ = 3 marks)  
2B)               In the fruit fly, recessive mutations in either of two independently assorting genes, brown and          (3)  
  purple, prevent the synthesis of red pigment in the eyes. Thus, homozygotes for either of these  
  mutations have brownish-purple eyes. However, heterozygotes for both of these mutations have  
  dark red, that is, wild-type eyes. If such double heterozygotes are intercrossed,  
  What kinds of progeny will be produced and in what proportions?  
  (1+2 = 3 marks)  
2C)               In rabbits, the dominant allele B causes black fur and the recessive allele b causes brown fur; for an (4)  
  independently assorting gene, the dominant allele R causes long fur and the recessive allele r  
  causes short fur. A homozygous rabbit with long, black fur is crossed with a rabbit with short, brown  
  fur, and the offspring are intercrossed.  
  (a) In the F2 , what proportion of the rabbits will be with long and black fur?  
  (b) In the F2 , what proportion of the rabbits with long, black fur will be homozygous for both genes?  
  (c) Mention the genotypic ratio in the F2.  
  (1+1+2 = 4 marks)  
3A)               A cell-free extract is prepared from Type IIIS pneumococcal cells. What effect will treatment of this (3)  
  extract with  
  (a) protease,  
  (b) RNase, and  
  (c) DNase have on its subsequent capacity to transform recipient Type IIR cells to Type IIIS? Why?  
3B)               Indicate whether each of the following statements about the structure of DNA is true or false. (Each (3)  
  letter is used to refer to the concentration of that base in DNA.)  
  $$(a) A + T = G + C$$  
  
  Page #1

$$(b) A = G; C = T$$  
  $$(c) A/T = C/G$$  
  $$(d) T/A = C/G$$  
  $$(e) G/C = 1$$  
  $$(f) A = T within each single strand.$$  
3C)   (a) Explain the experiment performed by Griffith on Streptococcus pneumonia.   (4)  
  (b) Name the three scientists who followed up Griffith's experiments.  
  (c) What did they conclude from this experiment?  
  (1½+½+1 4 marks)  
4A)   Explain Darwinism                                                              (3)  
4B)   Provide three evidences of evolution                                           (3)  
4C)   Explain hierarchical levels of organization in living systems                  (4)  
5A)   Logically explain the bioinspiration that silenced the bullet train            (3)  
5B)   Why engineers are trying to understand mechanisms of living systems?           (3)  
5C)   Construct bioinspiration ideas for (1) Impact resistance (2) Wind mill         (4)  
  Build bioinspiration ideas from (A) Shark skin (B) Termite  
  
  
  -----End-----
